title: The patient who could only repeat “tan”

probes.question: Which syllable could Leborgne repetitively produce?
True or false: a lesion was discovered on the surface of Leborgne's left frontal lobe.

image.alt: Side view of a 3D brain inside a translucent skull with Broca's area highlighted in red in the left frontal lobe.
image.credit: Polygon data were generated by Database Center for Life Science(DBCLS)[2]. / Wikimedia Commons

panels.text: Louis Victor Leborgne was a patient of Pierre Paul Broca's. At 30 years old, he was almost completely unable to produce any words or phrases.
When asked a question, he was only able to repetitively produce the syllable “tan”.
After his death, a neurosyphilitic lesion was discovered on the surface of his left frontal lobe.
These two cases led Broca to believe that speech was localized to this particular area. Since then, the approximate region he identified has become known as Broca’s area.
